comment: Copy the pieces you want into ~/.pi/agent/keybindings.json. The "modal" block is read by the modal_keybinds extension; pi itself ignores it. The extension ships with NO built-in bindings — the modal menu shows exactly what you configure here (old configs still merge over the empty defaults).
comment2: The app.message.copy rebind below is optional. Prefixes are handled by the extension directly (not pi shortcuts), so nothing conflicts and no warning is printed. But if you leave app.message.copy on ctrl+x, the modal owns ctrl+x while the editor is focused and copy would be unreachable from there, so moving it elsewhere is recommended.
comment3: The "action" type invokes an app action by name: it looks up the handler pi registered on the focused editor's actionHandlers map and calls it directly — no keybinding lookup, so it works even if the action is unbound or rebound. See ctrl+x m/x/e/l/n below: model selector, copy, external editor, and session new/resume are all pi's own handlers, reused with zero duplication.
comment4: Handler names containing a ':' are event channels on pi.events (pi's shared extension event bus): modal_keybinds emits { ctx, pi } on that channel and any other extension may subscribe. No registry or global state — the name is the contract. Use this for things that are NOT app actions (e.g. undo/redo handled by the undo-redo extension); app actions go through the "action" type instead.
comment5: timeout_ms: how long to wait for the next key before cancelling. Omit it for NO timeout — the modal waits until you pick a key, press escape, or ctrl+c.
